spec.name: carry-ladder-norot-v1
spec.limitations: No rotation step, so bits within a byte are never permuted; mixing relies only on addition carries, which affect more significant bits than they read. I expect the whole eight-step map to collapse to a short closed-form byte expression (an alternating add/xor normal form) that can be written down and inverted symbolically rather than attacked, and it is again per-byte with no key input and no cross-byte diffusion.
spec.math: Each step is a bijection on {0..255}: add_c is translation x -> x+c mod 256 with inverse x -> x-c; xor_c is the involution x -> x XOR c. The composite of eight bijections is bijective and inverts by reversing order with add-key/add replaced by 256-n and xor unchanged. The map is not Z/256-affine (XOR is not linear over that ring), but it lies in the alternating add/xor normal form, so it can be expanded symbolically into one arithmetic expression.
spec.assumptions: Byte-aligned input; ops applied independently to each byte; no rotation available, so no intra-byte bit permutation is assumed; operands are literal constants baked into the program, not an external key.
